scope: CORRECTION of the 'two cursors' idea: [+0x1C] is the BYTE index and [+0x20] is the BIT position of the SAME stream - they are two views of one position

the_bit_reader_0x447190.0x447194: cmp [edx],0 ; je 0x4471A0 - return -1 if the stream is already in error
the_bit_reader_0x447190.0x4471A0: ecx = [edx+0x20] & 7 - the bit offset inside the current byte
the_bit_reader_0x447190.0x4471B5: cmp eax,esi ; jl 0x4471C7 - overrun sets [edx]=1 and returns -1
the_bit_reader_0x447190.0x4471C7: esi = eax*8 ; [edx+0x20] = esi ; [edx+0x1C] = eax+1 - when starting a new byte, the byte index advances and the bit position is set to byte*8
the_bit_reader_0x447190.0x4471DF: eax = ebx >> 3 - the byte index derived from the bit position

the_correction: the earlier note said the snapshot has 'two independent cursors, one in bits and one in bytes'
that is WRONG: [+0x20] is the absolute bit position and [+0x1C] is the byte index of the SAME stream, and the bit reader keeps them consistent
the byte reader 0x66ED70 also advances [+0x1C], so a byte read moves the same position forward by one byte
so there is ONE logical position, exposed in two units - and mixing the two units is what made the earlier interpretation look strange
what_this_gives_us: [+0x20] at 0x671650 entry is EXACTLY the bit index of the first gate bit
the second gate bit is [+0x20]+1, and the count byte is read at the byte containing [+0x20] after those two bits
so one more probe reading [+0x20] pins both gate bits precisely, and that is the last unknown before the gates can be set deliberately
